statement: Fix θ>0, φ>7/2, Φ>φ+1, Cσ>0; let t=log log T and let X and η=σ−1/2 be deterministic and satisfy T^{1/t^Φ}≤X≤T^{1/t^φ}, 0<η≤Cσ t^Φ/log T, η log X/t→∞. For one τ uniform on [T,2T] let M_T=max_{|h|≤(log T)^θ}log|ζ(σ+i(τ+h))|. The author claims P(M_T−u_T≤x)→exp(−κ_θ exp(−2√(1+θ)x)) for every real x, where u_T is the specified one-point Haar-prime-phase quantile and 0<κ_θ<∞ is a microscopic Gaussian-profile lattice limit. The same maximum law is claimed separately in the Euler and Haar fields. No RH assumed, no global range maximum, no critical-line inference, no claim about zero statistics or whole-field limits.

Under the preceding displacement and cutoff assumptions, sup_{|h|≤(log T)^θ}|log|ζ(σ+i(τ+h))|−Re Σ_{p^j≤X}p^{-j(σ+i(τ+h))}/j| is o_P(1). The maximum transfer is a consequence of this uniform approximation and a separate limit theorem for the arithmetic Euler field. The claim uses ordinary zero-density control on a random rectangle, no RH and no fixed global zero-free half-plane.
